text:
Alex (eng): Quick heads-up — we're planning a small but technically breaking change in the partner SDKs: the default retry cap param `max_retries` will change from 5 -> 3 in SDK v4. Need coordination with partners and marketplace vendors.

Maria (partnerships): Timeline? who are the canary partners?

Alex (eng): Targeting canary rollout next Weds (2/8) with a 7-day canary window, then broad ramp over 2 weeks if metrics look good. Canary partners: Rachel's SI team, AcmeCloud, and one marketplace vendor (TBD).

Sam (sdk): We'll add a compat lifeline env var so partners can opt into old behavior during the window. Example: 
```bash
export REDWOOD_SDK_COMPAT_MAX_RETRIES=5  # keeps old 5-retry default
# OR set via client config:
client = RedwoodClient(max_retries_override=5)
```
This will ship as a toggle in v4.0.0-canary.

Jordan (pm): Communication plan: notify canary partners 48h before canary, publish breaking-change notice on marketplace listing, and include migration notes + snippet above. Also propose a short migration script for server-side wraps.

Lee (eng-infra): Gating metrics for canary: error-rate delta <= 0.5pp, 99th latency change <= 20ms, and token cost within +/- 3%. We'll auto-rollback if any metric exceeds thresholds for 4 consecutive hours. I'll wire charts and alerts.

Rachel (partner): FYI Rachel (partner) here — our on-prem integrator needs a 30d lifeline for regulators; 7 days won't cut it. Can we provide a formal exception process? Also want an SDK-side shim package we can pin.

Alex (eng): Yes — exception process: partners can request a temporary compat extension (30d max) via partners@redwood with justification; eng will produce a pinned shim build (signed) for marketplace/private repos. We'll track exceptions in the partner playbook.

Sam (sdk): For marketplace packages we'll publish two artifacts: `redwood-sdk@v4` (default new behavior) and `redwood-sdk@v4-compat-5-retries` (shim/pinned). We'll sign both and add a "compat badge" label for listed packages.

Maria (partnerships): I'll prepare partner-facing email + short one-pager: what changed, why, how to opt-out, how to request exceptions. Also include migration checklist and test command.

Jordan (pm): Migration checklist (short):
- Search for implicit reliance on default retry behavior in server handlers
- Add explicit `max_retries` where applicable
- Run canary smoke-tests (see below)
- If using on-prem bundles, request shim build

Sam (sdk): Smoke-test CLI: 
```bash
# basic smoke test against canary endpoint
redwood-smoke --host=https://canary.redwood.ai --apikey=$PARTNER_KEY --parallel=10 --duration=120s
```
This will surface retry regressions quickly (we simulate transient failures).

Lee (eng-infra): I'll create the canary release in our CI tonight and schedule compat-bot to open the canary channel. compat-bot: please create `#canary-sdk-v4` and post canary release notes.

compat-bot: Created channel #canary-sdk-v4, uploaded v4.0.0-canary build, and scheduled metric dashboards.

Rachel (partner): Thanks. We'll try the canary but please escalate if we see a >1% uptick in customer error pages. Also please include signed shim artifact for our security team to ingest.

Alex (eng): Agreed — signed shim will be prepared. Next steps: Maria send partner email by EOD today, Sam cut canary build tonight, Lee wire dashboards, Jordan draft rollback playbook. We'll reconvene in this thread at canary start. :thumbsup:

Maria (partnerships): Draft ready, sending now. cc @Rachel (partner) for review.

Sam (sdk): Canary artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-canaries/sdk/v4.0.0-canary-2026-02-08.tar.gz

Lee (eng-infra): Dashboards up. Alert thresholds set.

Jordan (pm): Rollback playbook in the repo: https://goto/redwood/partner-rollback-playbook (short link).

Rachel (partner): Acked. We'll monitor from our side and report any customer impact within the first 6h.

Alex (eng): Thanks all. Keeping this short and focused. Will post a summary after canary ends. :white_check_mark:
